what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat plaque psoriasis, a skin condition that causes red, scaly, itchy patches on your skin. It contains two active ingredients that work together: calcipotriene slows down the overgrowth of skin cells, and betamethasone dipropionate is a steroid that reduces redness, swelling, and itching.
how_to_take: Apply a thin layer of this medicine directly to the affected skin areas only. Gently rub it in until it disappears into the skin. Wash your hands thoroughly after applying unless you are treating your hands. Do not apply to your face, groin, armpits, or inside skin folds unless your doctor specifically tells you to. Do not cover treated areas with tight bandages or wraps unless instructed by your doctor. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or nose. If accidental contact occurs, rinse well with water.
dosing: For most adults, apply once daily to the affected areas. Do not use more than directed by your doctor. The foam or spray form (Enstilar) is typically used once daily for up to 4 weeks. The ointment or cream form (Taclonex or Wynzora) may be used once daily for up to 8 weeks. Do not use on more than 30% of your body surface area. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing may vary.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular routine. Do not apply extra medicine to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep away from heat, open flames, and direct sunlight. The foam form (Enstilar) is flammable — do not use near fire, flames, or while smoking, and do not puncture or throw the canister into fire. Keep all forms of this medicine out of the reach of children. Do not freeze. Keep the cap or lid tightly closed when not in use.
what_to_avoid: Avoid applying this medicine to your face, underarms, groin, or areas where skin rubs together unless your doctor tells you otherwise. Do not use on broken, infected, or severely irritated skin. Avoid using other skin products, lotions, or medicines on the same areas unless your doctor approves. Limit exposure of treated skin to sunlight or tanning beds, as this medicine may make your skin more sensitive to UV light. Do not use more than the recommended amount or for longer than prescribed, as overuse of the steroid ingredient can cause skin thinning and other side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience: skin irritation, burning, stinging, or redness that is severe or gets worse; signs of a skin infection such as increased warmth, swelling, oozing, or pus; stretch marks or thinning of the skin; unusual weight gain, swelling, or fatigue (possible signs of too much steroid being absorbed); high levels of calcium in your blood, which may cause nausea, vomiting, weakness, confusion, or excessive thirst and urination; or if your psoriasis is not improving or gets worse after a few weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Many patients start to see improvement in their skin within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. Maximum benefit is usually seen after 4 to 8 weeks of regular use. Do not stop using this medicine early just because your skin looks better — continue using it as directed unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Children and teenagers: Safety and effectiveness in children under 12 years old have not been established. Use with extra caution in children, as they may absorb more of the medicine through the skin. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as steroid-containing products may carry risks. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Discuss with your doctor before breastfeeding while using this product. Elderly patients: Older adults may have thinner skin and should use this medicine carefully to avoid increased absorption of the steroid ingredient.
